answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by requiring each identity to carve a relic from original work that cannot be copied. The relic is checked against a karst of prior answers from the same author, so near-duplicates are rejected on the ledger. A crystal of independent graders then attests only the fresh carving. Forging many identities therefore costs one full original generation and external verification cycle per identity instead of a single cheap template.
